newsitem.title: USA: Regis Q2 hurt by retail product sales.
newsitem.headline: Regis Q2 hurt by retail product sales.

text.p: Regis Corp, which operates and franchises hair salons, said Tuesday its results for the fiscal second quarter were hurt by a softer than expected hair care product sales due to competition.

"Despite the growth in earnings, our second quarter operating performance was below plan, due largely to an unexpected softening in retail product sales resulting from increased competition," Paul Finkelstein, chief executive officer, said in a statement.
"As a result, we are now redoubling our efforts to sharpen our retail product assortments and presentations," Finkelstein added.
He said Regis now expects total revenues, combined gross margin and operating margin in the second half of fiscal 1997 will be in line with those reported for the first half.

Earlier, Regis reported a second quarter net loss of $0.38 a share, compared with a loss of $0.17 a year ago. Excluding chares related to its merger with Supercuts and restructuring efforts, Regis earned $0.21 a share, up from $0.16 a year ago.

"The Supercuts division is performing in line with our expectations, enjoying second quarter system-wide, same-store sales increases of 4.3 percent," Finkelstein said. "The integration of the Supercuts business, as well as other salons recently acquired, is proceeding according to plan. We will continue to focus on our core strategy of growing through same-store sales improvement, new salon construction and acquisition as we further consolidate the hair salon industry."
